subject: text labels for scatter plot points

messages.author: 496499cefe2ae056
messages.subject: text labels for scatter plot points
parts:
Hi,

I created a scatter plot from the row and column coordinates of a
correspondence analysis using package ca. I basically created two data
frames, one for the row coordinates and one for the column coordinates,
and then stacked them using rbind. I then drew a scatter plot using
this combined data frame. The plot looks fine except that the labels
for the points are not appealing. Some run off the edge of the plot on
the right, some on the left. All labels are too close to the points and
all are the same size and color. I'd like to control

1. where the labels are placed (Stata has a feature that allows
placing the labels around the points based on a clock analogy with
3 o'clock as the default; all labels can be set individually by
specifying a clock position)
2. the size of individual labels (some small and others slightly larger)
3. the color of individual labels (row points red and column points
green, for example for my correspondence analysis combined data frame)

Finally, how do I pick different symbols for the points rather than just
the default black dots? For example, I'd like the row points to be red
squares and the column points to be green triangles.

Thanks,

Walt

> combined data frame.  The plot looks fine except that the labels for the

>
>  1. where the labels are placed (Stata has a feature that allows
>     placing the labels around the points based on a clock analogy with
>     3 o'clock as the default; all labels can be set individually by
>     specifying a clock position)
You can use the angle aesthetic for this.
>  2. the size of individual labels (some small and others slightly larger)

>  3. the color of individual labels (row points red and column points
>     green, for example for my correspondence analysis combined data frame)

> Finally, how do I pick different symbols for the points rather than just the
> default black dots?  For example, I'd like the row points to be red squares
> and the column points to be green triangles.

See the shape aesthetic and scale_shape_manual.

And as always, it's always easier to provide help if you provide a
minimal reproducible example.
